title: XOR and XNOR from a 2:1 MUX
tasks: Use mux2 instances only (plus ~b): no ^ operator.
x = a XOR b, xn = a XNOR b.
Run: the testbench checks all four input combinations.
problem: A favourite at Qualcomm, NVIDIA, Google and Micron: build XOR and XNOR using only 2:1 multiplexers (one inverter on b is allowed).

title: AND, OR, NAND and NOT from MUXes
q: \b(and|or|nand|nor|not|inverter|gates?)\b.{0,25}\b(using|from|with)\b.{0,15}(mux|multiplexer)|(mux|multiplexer)e?s?.{0,25}\b(create|make|build|implement|design)\b.{0,20}\b(nand|and|or|gates?|inverter)\b|basic gates.{0,20}mux|gate implementation using mux|block one input of an and
tasks: Use only mux2 instances and the constants 1'b0 and 1'b1.
and_o, or_o, nand_o and not_a.
Run until PASS.
problem: Asked at AMD, Marvell, Cadence, Broadcom and Qualcomm: build the basic gates from 2:1 multiplexers and the constants 0 and 1.

title: Full adder from 2:1 MUXes
tasks: Use only mux2 instances and constants (no ^ & | operators).
sum = a ^ b ^ cin, cout = majority(a, b, cin).
Hint: p = a ^ b; then sum = p ? ~cin : cin and cout = p ? cin : a.
problem: AMD and others ask: build a full adder with nothing but 2:1 multiplexers.

title: 3-input XOR from one 4:1 MUX
tasks: Drive sel with {a, b}.
Choose each data input from c, ~c, 0 or 1.
Run until PASS.
problem: From Qualcomm: implement y = a ^ b ^ c with a single 4:1 multiplexer (an inverter on c is allowed).

title: 8:1 and 16:1 MUX from 2:1 MUXes
tasks: mux8: 8 inputs, 3-bit select, built from mux2 instances (7 of them).
mux16: 16 inputs, 4-bit select (15 mux2s, or two mux8s and one mux2).
Run until PASS.
problem: Synopsys, Samsung, Marvell and Intel all ask it: build bigger multiplexers from 2:1 MUXes, and say how many you need.

title: XOR from NOR only and from NAND only
q: xor.{0,20}only nor|xor.{0,20}only nand|universal gates|nor gate only from nand|nor.{0,20}from nand|or gate using nand|realize logic functions with universal
tasks: x_nor: XOR using only the nor primitive (5 gates).
x_nand: XOR using only the nand primitive (4 gates).
Run until PASS.
problem: Classic campus question: NAND and NOR are universal. Build XOR from NOR gates only, and from NAND gates only.

title: D latch from a MUX
q: latch.{0,30}(mux|multiplexer)|most basic sequential|asynchronous feedback loop|level-triggered versus edge
tasks: q follows d while en = 1 and holds while en = 0.
Use one mux2 whose output feeds back into one data input.
Run until PASS.
problem: ARM and Intel ask how storage appears from combinational logic: feed a 2:1 MUX output back to its own input and you have a latch.

title: Count the 1s with full adders
q: (count|how many).{0,20}(1s|ones|1's|logic 1).{0,40}(adder|full)|5 inputs that count|count the number of 1
tasks: Five 1-bit inputs, 3-bit count.
Use the given ha and fa modules only.
A full adder is a 3:2 compressor: it adds three bits of the same weight.
problem: NVIDIA and Marvell ask: count how many of the inputs are 1, using only half and full adders.

title: Equality and 2-bit comparator from 1-bit comparators
tasks: eq: 1 when a == b for any WIDTH (XNOR each bit, AND them all).
cmp2: gt, eq, lt for 2-bit numbers using two cmp1 instances and a few gates.
Run until PASS.
problem: Texas Instruments and Qualcomm ask: check two N-bit numbers for equality, then build a 2-bit magnitude comparator from 1-bit comparators.

title: Max and sort of three numbers
tasks: lo <= mid <= hi for unsigned 8-bit a, b, c.
Use three compare-and-swap stages (a sorting network), no loops.
max is hi.
problem: ARM asks for the maximum of three numbers in hardware, and AMD asks to sort with 2-input sorters. Build a 3-input sorting network.

title: Multiply by a constant: x5 and x47
q: multipl(y|ies).{0,30}(by|times) ?(5|47|a constant)|by 47|square of a number|multiply a 2-bit
tasks: y5 = x * 5 and y47 = x * 47 for an 8-bit unsigned x.
Use shifts, + and - only: no * operator.
Pick output widths that never overflow.
problem: NVIDIA asked for a circuit that multiplies by 47; Marvell for x5. Constant multipliers are built from shifts and adds, not a multiplier.

title: BCD digit times 5
tasks: tens and ones are BCD digits of d * 5 (0 to 45).
There is a trick that needs no adder at all: look at d * 5 for even and odd d.
Run until PASS.
problem: From an Intel CPU verification interview: take a 4-bit BCD digit (0 to 9) and output the result times 5 as two BCD digits.

title: Bit widths, signed multiply and sign extension
q: bits are needed to hold|bit width needed|sign-extend|truncate|multiply two signed|negative numbers stored|two's complement|smallest positive and negative|signed 16-bit
tasks: mac: y = a * b + c for unsigned 8-bit a, b, c. Give y the smallest width that never overflows.
smul: product of two signed 8-bit numbers.
sext: sign-extend an 8-bit value to 16 bits.
problem: Marvell asked how many bits A*B+C needs for 8-bit operands, and how to truncate and sign-extend. Get the widths and signedness right.

title: Bit tricks: power of 2, bit reverse, lowest set bit, min without if
q: power of 2|power of two|reverses the bit|reverse.{0,10}bits|bit manipulation|extract bits|position of every 1|smaller of two integers without|without (an|using) if|lowest set bit|swap two (variables|values)
tasks: pow2 = 1 when x is a power of 2 (x != 0 and x & (x - 1) == 0).
rev = x with its bit order reversed.
low1 = x with only its lowest 1 kept (x & -x).
mn = min(x, z) without if or ?: (use a mask).
problem: One-liners interviewers love (Maxlinear, Micron, Marvell, Intel, Cadence): power-of-2 check, bit reversal, isolating the lowest 1, and min of two numbers without if.

title: Add 64-bit numbers with one 32-bit adder
tasks: On start, latch a and b. Cycle 1 adds the low halves; cycle 2 adds the high halves plus the saved carry.
Raise done for one cycle with the 65-bit result in sum (bit 64 is the carry out).
Use a single 32-bit add expression, reused in both cycles.
problem: AMD asked how to add two 64-bit numbers when you only have a 32-bit adder. Do it in two cycles, carrying between them.

title: Edge detectors and a one-cycle delay
q: edge.?trigger.{0,30}variation|rising edge|falling edge|detects a rising|edge detect|delays a signal by one clock|pulse detector
tasks: d1 is sig delayed by one clock.
rise, fall and any are one-cycle pulses from sig and d1.
Run until PASS.
problem: Cadence, Apple and NVIDIA ask for edge detection: delay a signal by one clock, then pulse on its rising edge, falling edge or any edge.

title: Sticky register
tasks: q = 0 in reset.
q becomes 1 the clock after set = 1, then holds 1.
Run until PASS.
problem: NVIDIA's new-grad screen: design a sticky register that goes to 1 when set and stays 1 until reset, whatever set does afterwards.

title: Odd clock divider with 50% duty cycle
q: divide.{0,12}(by )?(3|5|7|three)|divided by three|divide-by-[357]|clock divider|clock dividers|frequency divider|divide a 500|duty cycle
tasks: clk_out period = N input clocks, high for exactly N/2 clocks (half-cycle resolution).
Count on the rising edge; use one extra flop on the falling edge.
The testbench runs N = 3 and N = 5 and measures high and low time.
problem: Divide-by-3 with 50% duty is one of the most reported questions (Marvell, Broadcom, NXP, TI, Cadence). Build a general odd divider: N = 3, 5, 7...

title: Counters that skip values or count a range
q: skip|counts from 7 to 11|count(s|er)? (from )?7 to 11|mod-15|mod 15|mod-n counter|modulo-50|mod-3 counter|count-to-5|up/down counter|counter.{0,20}minimum number of flops|wrapping counter|parameterized counter
tasks: skip: counts 1, 2, 6, 7, 9, 10, 11, 12, 13, 14 and wraps to 1. Reset value 1.
range: counts 7, 8, 9, 10, 11 and wraps to 7. Reset value 7.
Run until PASS.
problem: Micron asked for a mod-15 counter that skips 0, 3, 4, 5 and 8; Samsung for a counter from 7 to 11. Build both.

title: Fibonacci generator: one number per cycle
tasks: After reset, f outputs 0, 1, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, ... one per clock.
Use two registers; no memory, no loop.
16-bit output: the testbench checks the first 24 numbers.
problem: Fibonacci in hardware came up at Marvell, Juniper, TI and Intel: output the next Fibonacci number every clock.

title: Moving average of the last 4 samples
q: moving average|average of the values|average between
tasks: Shift in x on every clock (window starts as zeros after reset).
avg = (sum of the last 4 samples) / 4.
Keep a running sum: add the new sample, subtract the one that leaves. No 4-input adder needed.
problem: Groq asked for a moving average in Verilog. Keep the last four 8-bit samples and output their average every clock.

title: Sum of the previous two inputs, and a running sum
q: sum of the previous two|running sum|accumulator|cumulative sum
tasks: s2 = sum of the two inputs before the current one (0 for missing ones).
run = sum of all inputs before the current one.
Both come from registers: no combinational path from x.
problem: From a Texas Instruments interview: for a stream A0, A1, A2..., output A(k-1) + A(k-2) while A(k) arrives, then the sum of all previous inputs.

title: 8-bit maximal-length LFSR
tasks: Shift left; the new LSB is q[7] ^ q[5] ^ q[4] ^ q[3].
Reset to 8'h01 (never all zeros: the LFSR would lock).
The testbench checks the period is exactly 255.
problem: AMD asked to explain an LFSR. Build an 8-bit Fibonacci LFSR with taps 8, 6, 5, 4 that cycles through all 255 non-zero states.

title: Accumulate data per address
tasks: On valid, total[addr] <= total[addr] + data (same clock).
Back-to-back writes to the same address must both count.
rd_addr reads a total combinationally.
problem: NVIDIA asked for RTL that accumulates incoming data per address. Keep 8 running totals and add each valid input to its address.

title: Testbench clocks: 2 GHz, start after 100 ns
q: ^(?!.*divid).*(generate.{0,20}clock|clock (signal )?at a (given|certain) frequency|2 ghz|clock that stays off|clock generator|skewed clock|always, and using forever|timescale)
tasks: clk_a: 2 GHz (0.5 ns period) from time 0, starting low. Mind the timescale precision.
clk_b: 100 MHz, held at 0 until 100 ns, then toggling (first rising edge at 105 ns).
Write them in the clkgen module; the testbench measures both.
problem: Writing clocks is a classic screen question (AMD, Qualcomm, Meta, Synopsys): a 2 GHz clock, and a clock that stays low until 100 ns and then toggles.

title: 1011 detector, Mealy, overlapping
tasks: Mealy: det = 1 in the same cycle the final 1 arrives.
Overlapping: after a hit, continue from the matched suffix 1, not from the start.
Four states: S0, S1 (1), S10, S101.
problem: The single most reported FSM question: detect 1011 on a serial input, allowing overlaps (101011 contains one, 1011011 contains two).

title: 1011 detector, Moore, overlapping
q: moore.{0,40}(detect|sequence|1011)|mealy and moore|moore machines? that detect|draw a mealy|mealy or moore|types of finite state|mealy versus moore|between mealy and moore|between moore and mealy|convert one into the other|advantages of mealy
tasks: Five states; det = 1 while in the 'seen 1011' state.
det is high in the cycle after the final 1.
Keep overlaps: from S1011, a 0 goes to S10 and a 1 to S1.
problem: The follow-up every interviewer asks: now make it Moore. The output depends only on the state, so you need one more state and det comes one cycle later.

title: Serial divisible-by-5 and by-3 checker
tasks: Keep the remainder, not the number: r_new = (2*r + bit) mod 5.
div5 = 1 when the remainder after this bit is 0 (Mealy).
Same for div3 with 3 states.
problem: Apple and NVIDIA ask: bits arrive MSB first; after each bit, say whether the number so far is divisible by 5 (and by 3).

title: Vending machine
tasks: One coin per cycle at most: n5 or n10 pulses.
vend pulses with the coin that reaches 15 or more; change = 1 when 20 was paid.
Credit returns to 0 after a vend.
problem: NVIDIA asked for a vending machine module. An item costs 15. Coins are 5 and 10. Vend when 15 or more is inserted and return 5 change on 20.

title: Round-robin arbiter, 4 requesters
tasks: grant is one-hot (or 0 when nobody requests), registered.
Search from the requester after the last winner, wrapping around.
The testbench checks fairness: a waiting requester is served within 4 grants.
problem: Round-robin arbiters came up at Qualcomm, Cisco, SiFive, Marvell and AMD. Four requesters share one resource; the last winner gets lowest priority next time.

title: Fixed-priority arbiter with async reset
tasks: grant is registered and one-hot: the lowest-numbered active request wins.
Asynchronous active-high reset clears grant immediately.
Run until PASS.
problem: AMD: requests R1 to R4 with R1 highest priority drive grants G1 to G4, with an asynchronous reset. Qualcomm asks for it next to round-robin.

title: Combination lock with alarm
tasks: On enter, compare code with the stored key (reset value 4'b1011).
Right code: unlocked = 1 and the wrong count clears. Wrong code: count; on the third wrong try alarm = 1 and stays 1 until reset.
While unlocked, set_key stores code as the new key and locks again.
problem: MaxLinear: unlock a safe on code 1011 and sound an alarm after three wrong tries. Intel added: let the owner change the code once it is open.

title: Glitch-free clock switch
tasks: Each clock gets an enable flop clocked on its own falling edge.
A clock's enable may only rise after the other clock's enable has fallen (cross-coupled).
clk_out = (clk0 & en0) | (clk1 & en1). The testbench measures every pulse.
problem: Intel SoC integration: switch between two unrelated clocks without producing a glitch (a pulse shorter than either clock's half period).

title: Pattern detector with a shift register
q: shift register|constant your state machine compares|grows from 6 to 100|implement a system that outputs 1
tasks: Shift din into a LEN-bit register each clock.
det = 1 when the last LEN bits equal PATTERN (after at least LEN bits).
The testbench uses LEN = 6 and LEN = 11.
problem: IMC asked what happens to a state machine when the pattern grows from 6 bits to 100. Answer: use a shift register and a comparator. Build a parameterized one.

title: FIFO depth: size it from the traffic
q: fifo depth|depth of (the )?(fifo|buffer)|deep must (the )?(fifo|buffer)|size (them|a fifo)|width of a buffer|how deep|fifo sizes
tasks: The FIFO is given. Only change DEPTH.
Too small: the testbench reports an overflow. Too big: it reports wasted entries.
Work it out first: words written during the burst minus words read in the same time.
problem: FIFO depth calculation is asked at AMD, Juniper, NVIDIA and Marvell. A writer bursts 80 words, one per clock; the reader takes one word every 2 clocks. Find the smallest depth that never overflows.

title: Cache address split: tag, index, offset
q: tag, index|tag,? index and offset|bits are tag|bits of a memory address|address into tag|cache bits
tasks: OFF_W = log2(line bytes); sets = size / (line * ways); IDX_W = log2(sets); TAG_W = 32 - IDX_W - OFF_W.
Split addr into tag, idx and off with those widths.
The testbench checks a 1 MB 8-way 64 B cache and a 32 KB 2-way 64 B cache.
problem: Asked at Intel, Qualcomm, AMD and SiFive: for a given cache size, line size and associativity, how many bits are tag, index and offset? Make the hardware compute the split.

title: Direct-mapped cache with dirty bits
q: build a cache|implement a cache|how a cache works|cache works|dirty (bit|line)|write-back|cache hit|cache memory|cache system|what is (a )?cache|cache, and why|cache line
tasks: Address: 4-bit offset, 4-bit index, 8-bit tag (16-bit addresses).
On each access: hit = valid and tag match. On a miss, allocate the line; if the old line was valid and dirty, pulse wb (write-back).
Writes set dirty; reads of a newly filled line leave it clean.
problem: 'How would you build a cache?' (Marvell, NVIDIA, Arm). Build the tag store of a 16-line direct-mapped write-back cache: hit/miss, valid and dirty bits, and write-backs.

title: MESI coherence state machine
tasks: Local: rd (with shared = another cache has it) and wr. Snooped: bus_rd and bus_rdx (another cache wants to write).
I -rd-> E or S (shared); I -wr-> M; E -wr-> M; S -wr-> M (sends an upgrade).
Snooped bus_rd: M and E go to S (M flushes). Snooped bus_rdx: everything goes to I (M flushes).
problem: MESI is asked at Apple, Arm, Intel, NVIDIA and Qualcomm. Build the per-line state machine for one cache on a snooping bus.

title: LRU replacement for a 4-way set
tasks: Each way has a 2-bit age; 0 = most recent, 3 = least recent.
On an access to way w: ways younger than w age by one, w becomes 0.
victim = the way whose age is 3.
problem: AMD asked to code LRU for a cache; NVIDIA asked about eviction algorithms. Track recency of 4 ways and always point at the least recently used one.

title: 1-write 2-read RAM from two 1W1R RAMs
q: 1w2r|1-write 1-read|two read ports|dual-port memory|block ram|memory primitive|ram module|memory designed
tasks: Write the same data to both copies on every write.
Read port A uses copy 0, port B uses copy 1.
Reads are synchronous (data one clock after the address).
problem: AMD platform emulation: combine two 1-write 1-read block RAMs into a RAM with one write port and two read ports.

title: CRC-8 checker
tasks: Bits arrive MSB first, one per clock with valid.
crc <= {crc[6:0], 1'b0} ^ (fb ? 8'h07 : 0) where fb = crc[7] ^ bit.
After a message followed by its CRC, the register is 0: ok = 1.
problem: Intel asked for a CRC error checker in Verilog; Marvell asked how a receiver knows a codeword is bad. Build a serial CRC-8 (polynomial x^8 + x^2 + x + 1).

title: Interrupt controller
tasks: A rising edge on src[i] sets pending[i] (pending stays set until acknowledged).
irq = 1 when any pending & ~mask; id = the lowest-numbered such source (highest priority).
ack clears pending[id].
problem: Qualcomm asked how to design an interrupt controller; Infineon, TI and Arm asked how a CPU handles several interrupts. Build an 8-source controller with mask, priority and acknowledge.

title: fork/join: kill B when any finishes
tasks: Start A to D with fork ... join_any so you resume at the first finish.
Stop B with disable on its named block, then wait fork for the rest.
The testbench checks B never finishes and Done comes after A, C and D.
problem: Amazon asked: four processes A, B, C, D run in parallel. When any of them finishes, kill B; when all the others have finished, print Done. Qualcomm and NXP ask the fork-join variants.

title: randc by hand: a shuffled deck
tasks: fill a deck with 0..N-1, shuffle it with Fisher-Yates using $urandom_range.
next() returns the next card; when the deck runs out, reshuffle.
The testbench draws 5 rounds and checks every round is a permutation, and that rounds differ.
problem: NVIDIA and Arm asked to implement randc without the keyword; Qualcomm asked to shuffle an array fairly. Build a class that returns 0 to N-1 once each per round, in random order.

title: Constraint puzzles: unique, sum, alternate even/odd
q: ^(?!.*timing)(?!.*\bsdc\b).*(constraint|unique values|phone number|add k elements|even and odd|randomi[sz])
tasks: u: 6 values in 0..15, all different, without the unique keyword (compare every pair).
s: 5 values in 0..20 whose sum is exactly 40.
eo: 8 values in 0..99 alternating even, odd, even...
phone: 10 digits, first digit 6 to 9.
problem: Constraint coding is in almost every DV interview (Cadence, Meta, Qualcomm, Intel, Amazon). Solve four classics in one class.

title: Scoreboard for an out-of-order DUT
tasks: expect_item(id, data) records an outstanding transaction.
check(id, data) finds it by ID in any order, counts a match, a data mismatch or an unexpected ID, and removes it.
report() flags transactions that never came back.
problem: Amazon asked for a scoreboard for an out-of-order DUT; Apple for a scoreboard against a reference model. Responses come back in any order, matched by ID.

title: Merge two sorted arrays
tasks: merge() fills queue c with every element of a and b in ascending order.
Walk both with two indexes; take the smaller head each time.
Do not call sort().
problem: NVIDIA: write SystemVerilog that merges two sorted arrays into one sorted array, in one pass.
